newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses hold gains despite weaker Dow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses hold gains despite weaker Dow.

text.p: European stock markets continued to hold strong gains on Wednesday afternoon, even after the Dow Jones Industrial Average opened nearly flat, failing to extend Tuesday's steep rally.

In currency markets, the dollar dipped after an unexpected 0.6 percent drop in May U.S. durable goods orders added credibility to perceptions that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will keep U.S. interest rates steady at its July 1-2 meeting.
"Initially, the durable goods report should pressure the dollar," a trader at a French bank in New York said. "Dollar/yen should resume its slide and may retest the overnight low."
The dollar shed a yen overnight after the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan report showed that large manufacturing firms were more optimistic than expected.

Results from the U.S. Treasury's $11.5 billion, five-year government debt auction later on Wednesday would also be key in determining the near-term interest rate direction and thus, the dollar and the Dow's moves.
With U.S. analysts viewing U.S. five-year notes as still expensive, they said treasury prices could ease a bit more before the auction and weigh on the dollar and Dow.
"A lot for the dollar will depend on what bonds and the Dow do today," the trader in New York said.
Although the Dow's initial softness failed to drag European stocks lower, they remained off their peaks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 22.39 points at 7,735.67 after almost an hour.

France's CAC-40 index was off its record high hit earlier with help from news that Compagnie Bancaire had offered to buy out its units Cardif CDF.PA and Locabail for a maximum three billion francs ($515 million).
French banking stocks jumped on the back of Cie Bancaire's gain of nearly 7.5 percent, traders said.
London's FTSE-100 index also shrugged off Wall Street, lifted by hopes that Halifax Plc will make a share buy-back and bid talk surrounding Abbey National Plc.
Boots Co Plc also rose as Merrill Lynch repeated its positive stance after meeting with the retail chain.
The British government's debt auction earlier of two billion pounds matched analysts' expectations and also lent support to London stocks.
But the FTSE's rise was expected to remain restrained before the first budget of Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on July 2.
"Until we get rid of the clouds surrounding Gordon Brown's maiden budget, we'll not make any great progress," said NatWest equity strategist David McBain.
Germany's DAX index was firm, but its record high at 3,798.94 reached on June 20 remained elusive.
CURRENCIES AT 1410 GMT
The dollar was at 113.83 yen and 1.7236 marks, compared with 114.75 yen and 1.7235 marks in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 34.7 points at 4,631.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 64.64 points at 2,849.40.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 42.69 points at 3,798.51.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at 1500 GMT at $338.45 against $338.90 at Tuesday's close.
